name: RAGBRAI
unique: Thirty thousand riders cross Iowa in seven days, eating pie in church basements and sleeping in host towns that compete to throw the best party.
buzz: It is a rolling festival more than a race; training matters and the heat is real. Register early or join a charter.

name: Iowa State Fair
unique: The fair that invented the corn dog, with a butter cow, the largest livestock show in the country and a pork chop on a stick that draws pilgrims.
buzz: People plan vacations around it; the food is the attraction. Parking is easier than at most fairs.

name: Effigy Mounds National Monument
unique: Two hundred prehistoric mounds shaped like bears, birds and lines on bluffs above the Mississippi, with trails through the woods.
buzz: The bear mounds are subtle but the setting is beautiful. The bluff trail is a real hike.

name: Living History Farms
unique: A 500 acre open air museum with an 1700s Ioway village, an 1850 farm, a 1900 farm and a small town, with interpreters in period dress.
buzz: The breadth of the three farms is the strength, and kids can help with chores. Allow three hours.

name: Amana Colonies
unique: Seven villages settled by German Pietists, with communal kitchens, woolen mills, furniture shops and family style restaurants.
buzz: The colonies are a good half day, with crafts and heavy German food. The woolen mill is the best stop.

name: Maquoketa Caves
unique: Six miles of trails connecting caves you can actually enter, including one with a 17-foot ceiling and a natural bridge, in the middle of Iowa farmland.
buzz: Bring a headlamp and clothes you don't mind ruining; the caves are unpaved and genuinely dark. Mud is part of the deal.

name: Pappajohn Sculpture Park
unique: A 4.4 acre downtown park with 30 large outdoor sculptures, free and open at all hours, next to the art center.
buzz: The scale is surprising for Des Moines and the park is easy to walk. Free.

name: Field of Dreams
unique: The actual cornfield and farmhouse from the film, with a maintained diamond where anyone can hit and ghosts of a century of baseball lore.
buzz: People arrive cynical and leave misty eyed; the movie site is free and the souvenir shop is reasonable. Combine with Dubuque.

name: Czech Village
unique: A neighborhood of Czech bakeries, a butcher, a museum and a riverfront, with kolaches and a national Czech and Slovak museum.
buzz: The kolaches are the reason and the museum is worth an hour. The river walk is a bonus.

name: Loess Hills
unique: A narrow band of wind deposited hills along the Missouri, with prairie ridges, sharp bluffs and a landscape found in only one other place on earth.
buzz: The ridges are best at sunrise and the prairie flowers peak in summer. Drive the back roads.

name: Brucemore
unique: A 1886 Queen Anne mansion with 26 acres of grounds, a carriage house and the story of the three families who owned it.
buzz: The house tour is personal and the gardens are free to walk. Check the event schedule.

name: Fenelon Place Elevator
unique: The world's shortest and steepest scenic railway, a 296 foot funicular up the bluff to a view over the Mississippi and three states.
buzz: The ride is short and the view is the reward. A dollar or two, and a local institution.

name: Greater Des Moines Botanical Garden
unique: A domed conservatory and outdoor gardens on the Des Moines River, with tropical plants, a bonsai collection and a cafe.
buzz: The dome is the winter escape and the river walk is pretty. Cheap and calm.

name: Grotto of the Redemption
customer: Road trippers, religious pilgrims, art people
unique: A priest spent forty years building a nine grotto monument out of petrified wood, geodes, agate and malachite, a folk art cathedral in a cornfield.
buzz: It is free, sincere and stranger than photos suggest; the mineral collection is genuinely impressive.

name: Iowa Avenue Literary Walk
unique: A self guided walk through a UNESCO City of Literature, with bronze reliefs of writers and quotes set into the sidewalks.
buzz: A quiet hour for readers, and the used bookshops and Prairie Lights are the stops.

name: Lewis and Clark Interpretive Center
unique: A museum on the Missouri telling the Corps of Discovery story, with a keelboat, a prairie garden and a view of the river.
buzz: The exhibits are well done and the river setting is the point. Good for kids studying the expedition.

name: Bridges of Madison County
unique: Six covered wooden bridges from the 1880s, still standing on gravel roads, made famous by a novel and a film and still the best reason to drive rural Iowa.
buzz: The bridges are lovely and the driving is the point; the annual festival in October draws crowds. Stop at a small town cafe.

name: Villisca Axe Murder House
customer: Ghost hunters, true crime fans, teens
unique: An unsolved 1912 family murder house preserved almost as it was, with bullet holes in the walls and overnight investigations if you want to stay.
buzz: The tour is matter of fact about a real tragedy; it is eerie rather than theatrical. Not for young kids.
